test_cases.summary: Check that the ICS justifies every recommendation declared not applicable or not met.
Assess from IXIT whether non-user-defined passwords used outside factory default are generated unique per device.
test_cases.outside_procedure_cues: A cleartext credential matching a public default-password list would hint at universal defaults; the conceptual case reviews only IXIT.

test_cases.summary: Look for undocumented password mechanisms, check user-defined passwords are enforced, and check generated passwords match the documented mechanism.
test_cases.outside_procedure_cues: Cleartext HTTP Basic, Telnet or MQTT logins and answering login services reveal password mechanisms; IXIT completeness cannot be judged.

test_cases.summary: Judge whether the documented generation of pre-installed passwords avoids regularities, common strings, links to public data, and low complexity.
Check that actual pre-installed passwords plausibly follow the documented generation mechanism.
test_cases.outside_procedure_cues: Pre-installed passwords sent in cleartext can be seen and checked for form; the property route is 5.1-2-1.

test_cases.summary: Determine from IXIT whether any machine-to-machine authentication relies on passwords.
Search for undocumented mechanisms and check whether M2M authentication accepts passwords.
Assess documented security guarantees, mechanism fitness, best-practice status and known attacks for authentication cryptography.
Check that the authentication cryptography actually used matches the documented cryptographic details.
test_cases.outside_procedure_cues: TLS versions, cipher suites and certificates of authentication channels are visible in handshakes (TLS 1.3 certificates encrypted).

test_cases.summary: Assess whether user authentication values can be changed and whether user information explains how, plainly.
Perform the documented change of user authentication values and verify old values fail and new ones work.
Assess whether documented brute-force countermeasures on network-addressable authentication make attacks impracticable.
test_cases.outside_procedure_cues: Repeated third-party login attempts reaching the device and its continued responses could hint at missing rate limiting; opportunistic and not used by the TS.

test_cases.summary: Discover undocumented network authentication mechanisms and attempt brute force against documented ones.
test_cases.outside_procedure_cues: Answering Telnet/HTTP admin/API services expose network authentication; third-party login floods could hint at rate-limit behaviour.

test_cases.summary: Assess whether the vulnerability disclosure policy is accessible to anyone without accounts or similar barriers.
Verify the VDP is public and contains contact details plus acknowledgement and status-update timelines.
Assess whether documented actions and time frames ensure timely handling of disclosed vulnerabilities, plus SO confirmation.
test_cases.outside_procedure_cues: Public advisory and CVE dates compared with observed firmware updates could indicate handling speed; the TS case reviews only IXIT.

test_cases.summary: Assess documented processes for monitoring, identifying and rectifying vulnerabilities, plus SO confirmation.
test_cases.outside_procedure_cues: Component version banners (SSDP SERVER, HTTP Server, TLS libraries) matched to public CVEs that persist across releases hint at weak monitoring.

test_cases.summary: Assess justifications for non-updatable components and apply the update-mechanism design review of 5.3-2-1.
test_cases.outside_procedure_cues: Observed update traffic shows some components are updatable; the conceptual case cannot use it.

test_cases.summary: Apply the functional update-misuse attacks of 5.3-2-2 to each referenced update mechanism.
test_cases.outside_procedure_cues: Observed update traffic (transport protection, version manifests) shows the attack surface but not whether misuse succeeds.

test_cases.summary: Assess whether the documented design of each update mechanism prevents attacker misuse.
test_cases.outside_procedure_cues: Firmware fetched over plaintext HTTP or from unexpected hosts bears on misuse resistance; the design review gives no way to use it.

test_cases.summary: Devise and execute attacks (MITM, rollback, tampered packages) to test whether update misuse is prevented.
test_cases.outside_procedure_cues: Plaintext update delivery observed on the wire would identify mechanisms where MITM testing is most relevant.

test_cases.summary: Assess whether each software component has at least one update mechanism simple for users to apply.
test_cases.outside_procedure_cues: Update downloads without visible user activity would suggest automatic application, i.e. simple updating; only a conceptual case exists.

test_cases.summary: Assess from IXIT whether at least one update mechanism can be configured to run automatically.
test_cases.outside_procedure_cues: Unattended update traffic suggests an automated mechanism; the conceptual case cannot use it.

test_cases.summary: Check in the DUT configuration that at least one update mechanism can be automated.
Identify automatic update mechanisms and check that consent to enable them is queried and honoured at initialisation.
During setup, verify consent is requested and the automatic update state follows the user's choice.
test_cases.outside_procedure_cues: Update-check traffic and unattended installs after a household's onboarding show whether an automatic mechanism is active.

test_cases.summary: Assess from IXIT whether update mechanisms check for security updates during or after initialisation.
test_cases.outside_procedure_cues: Periodic requests to update endpoints after setup would show update checking; the provision has only a conceptual case, so this evidence is unused.

test_cases.summary: For automatic update mechanisms, check documented user ability to enable, disable and postpone them.
Verify in the DUT configuration that users can enable, disable and postpone automatic updates.
test_cases.outside_procedure_cues: If a household disables auto-update, disappearance of unattended installs after later releases would hint the setting works.

test_cases.summary: For mechanisms with update notifications, check documented user ability to enable and disable them.
Verify in the DUT configuration that users can enable and disable update notifications.
Assess documented guarantees, fitness, best-practice status and known attacks for update cryptography.
test_cases.outside_procedure_cues: Image signature algorithms are not visible unless signature files travel in plaintext.

test_cases.summary: Assess whether documented security-update procedures and time frames enable timely deployment, plus confirmation.
test_cases.outside_procedure_cues: Gap between public vulnerability disclosure and observed firmware update arrival could indicate timeliness; the case reviews only procedures.

test_cases.summary: Assess whether updates are checked for authenticity and integrity, and whether the DUT itself performs the checks.
test_cases.outside_procedure_cues: Plaintext downloads may reveal accompanying signature or hash files in URLs or manifests, hinting that verification exists.

test_cases.summary: Mixed case: review update verification via a trust relationship and discover undocumented network update mechanisms.
test_cases.outside_procedure_cues: Update checks and downloads over plaintext HTTP or from unexpected hosts show network update paths and unauthenticated channels; signature use stays unknown.

test_cases.summary: Assess whether users are informed recognisably about required security updates, including risks mitigated.
Check whether users are notified when an update will disrupt basic functioning.
test_cases.outside_procedure_cues: Device offline gaps during update installs are observable, showing disruption occurs, but not whether users were told.

test_cases.summary: Assess whether the published support period can be found and understood by a non-expert user.
Verify the access route to the support period works as documented, is unrestricted, and actually defines the period.
Checks that the published explanation of why a device receives no updates, and how hardware replacement is supported, is clear to non-experts.
Verify access to rationale and replacement plan works as documented, is unrestricted, and covers period and method.
Assess whether the documented isolation method can remove the DUT from its network or place it in a closed environment.
test_cases.outside_procedure_cues: During internet outages, continued local LAN traffic hints whether main functions survive loss of connectivity.

test_cases.summary: Isolate the DUT as documented and check that only connectivity-related functions are lost.
test_cases.outside_procedure_cues: During internet outages traffic shows reconnect behaviour, but not whether the main function survives.

test_cases.summary: Assess whether the documented hardware replacement method is suitable.
Replace the hardware as documented and verify connectivity and functions are regained.
test_cases.outside_procedure_cues: If a household replaces a unit, the new device resuming the same cloud endpoints and local patterns would be observable.

test_cases.summary: Assess whether the model designation is clearly recognisable by label or user interface.
test_cases.outside_procedure_cues: SSDP/mDNS model names reveal a network-advertised model, which is not the label/UI the provision requires.

test_cases.summary: Obtain the model designation as documented and check it is plain text and matches IXIT.
test_cases.outside_procedure_cues: Plaintext model strings in discovery protocols could be compared with an expected designation.

test_cases.summary: Assess consistency of SSP types, adequacy of guarantees and protection schemes, and completeness of the SSP list.
test_cases.outside_procedure_cues: TLS client certificates, tokens or keys visible in traffic reveal security parameters the device must hold, relevant to list completeness.

test_cases.summary: Check that documented storage protection schemes for SSPs are actually implemented.
test_cases.outside_procedure_cues: Secrets sent in cleartext would hint at weak handling, though not at storage protection.

test_cases.summary: Check hard-coded identities are declared and that their documented protection provides tamper resistance.
test_cases.outside_procedure_cues: Stable identifiers persisting across resets (client certificate subjects, device IDs in plaintext, MAC-derived names) suggest hard-coded identities.

test_cases.summary: Check that tamper-resistance protection of hard-coded identities is implemented as documented.
Check hard-coded CSPs are documented and that their provisioning prevents their use in operation.
test_cases.outside_procedure_cues: Identical credentials across same-model devices, or a public CVE on hard-coded keys for the identified model, would indicate hard-coded CSPs.

test_cases.summary: Check that the documented provisioning replacing hard-coded CSPs is really applied during operation.
test_cases.outside_procedure_cues: Credentials or certificates seen during and after onboarding could show whether a factory secret is replaced.

test_cases.summary: Check CSPs for update verification and service communication are documented and generated unique per device with sound mechanisms.
test_cases.outside_procedure_cues: The same client certificate or credential seen on several devices of one model would suggest non-unique CSPs.

test_cases.summary: Desk review of documented secure channels for all secure communication: guarantees, mechanism fit, best-practice crypto per catalogue, no known feasible attack.
Check on the device that the crypto actually used on channels for all secure communication matches what the IXIT documents.
test_cases.outside_procedure_cues: Observed handshakes (versions, suites, certificates) could be compared with IXIT if supplied; without it they only feed the conceptual catalogue check.

test_cases.summary: Desk check that each listed network/security implementation was reviewed or evaluated and that the review covers its scope.
test_cases.outside_procedure_cues: Handshake fingerprints, protocol banners or User-Agent strings may hint at the library in use, which could be looked up in public certification lists.

test_cases.summary: Check that name and version of each reviewed implementation on the device match those in its review report.
test_cases.outside_procedure_cues: Server banners, User-Agent strings and TLS fingerprints may reveal library names/versions, unusable without the SO report.

test_cases.summary: Desk check that crypto-using components have a referenced update mechanism and that replacement side effects were considered.
test_cases.outside_procedure_cues: Observed update traffic shows an update channel exists but says nothing about crypto replaceability.

test_cases.summary: Desk review that network-reachable functions need authentication, that it distinguishes subjects, is protected, and authorization works.
Try accessing network functions unauthenticated, with bad credentials, and with proper rights; check authentication protection against IXIT.
test_cases.outside_procedure_cues: Observed certificates and handshake parameters protecting authentication are visible but the third bullet compares them with the IXIT.

test_cases.summary: Same desk review as 5.5-4-1, in all device states, limited to functions permitting security-relevant configuration changes.
Active authentication tests from 5.5-4-2 for configuration-changing functions, plus search for undocumented network logical interfaces.
test_cases.outside_procedure_cues: Services seen answering inbound connections or advertised via mDNS/SSDP reveal logical interfaces, but documentation completeness needs the IXIT.

test_cases.summary: Desk review of documented secure channels carrying critical security parameters: guarantees, mechanism fit, best-practice crypto per catalogue, no known feasible attack.
test_cases.outside_procedure_cues: Plaintext credentials observed in traffic would contradict the provision directly.

test_cases.summary: Check on the device that the crypto actually used on channels carrying critical security parameters matches what the IXIT documents.
test_cases.outside_procedure_cues: Plaintext credentials or tokens in traffic would contradict the provision, but this case only compares with IXIT.

test_cases.summary: Desk review of documented secure channels carrying critical security parameters over remotely accessible interfaces: guarantees, mechanism fit, best-practice crypto per catalogue, no known feasible attack.
test_cases.outside_procedure_cues: Plaintext credentials to remote endpoints would contradict the provision directly.

test_cases.summary: Check on the device that the crypto actually used on channels carrying critical security parameters over remote interfaces matches what the IXIT documents.
test_cases.outside_procedure_cues: Plaintext credentials sent to remote endpoints would contradict the provision, but this case only compares with IXIT.

test_cases.summary: Desk review that CSP management processes span the full lifecycle and that the SO confirms implementing them.
test_cases.outside_procedure_cues: Long-term observation of certificate validity periods, rotations and revocation checks hints at parts of the key life cycle.

test_cases.summary: Desk check that every enabled network interface and network-reachable logical interface has a valid documented purpose.
Check device interface status against documentation and look for undocumented network and logical interfaces.
test_cases.outside_procedure_cues: Services seen answering on the LAN or WAN indicate enabled logical interfaces; completeness needs IXIT 28.

test_cases.summary: Desk review of what each network logical interface reveals without authentication: correctly labelled and necessary.
test_cases.outside_procedure_cues: Whether each disclosed item is documented as security-relevant is unknowable without the IXIT.

test_cases.summary: Observe whether interfaces leak security-relevant information without authentication beyond what is documented.
test_cases.outside_procedure_cues: Firmware or kernel versions in SSDP, mDNS, DHCP or HTTP headers are visible unauthenticated disclosures, but undocumentedness needs IXIT.

test_cases.summary: Desk check that physical interfaces not needing exposure are casing-protected and disabled per documentation.
Inspect device for exposed physical interfaces, casing protection and enabled status, against documentation.
Desk check that debug interfaces have best-practice access control or a disable mechanism and correct default status.
test_cases.outside_procedure_cues: Network-reachable debug services such as ADB or telnet answering connections could hint at an enabled debug path.

test_cases.summary: On the device, verify debug interfaces are disabled or protected and find undeclared interfaces usable for debugging.
test_cases.outside_procedure_cues: Unauthenticated debug-like network services observed answering connections would be indicative only.

test_cases.summary: Desk check that physical-port debug interfaces are documented as physically protected by the device.
Physically verify that debug ports are protected by the device.
Desk check that each default-enabled software service is necessary for intended use per its description and justification.
test_cases.outside_procedure_cues: Observed answering services (telnet, ftp, rtsp) suggest enabled services whose necessity the conceptual case cannot test.

test_cases.summary: Desk judgement of whether documented code minimization techniques suitably reduce code to needed functionality.
test_cases.outside_procedure_cues: Banners or advertised services revealing unneeded bundled components hint at unminimized code.

test_cases.summary: Desk judgement of whether documented privilege controls support separation of duty, need to know and least privilege.
Desk check that documented memory access control mechanisms are hardware-level and actually control memory access.
Desk review that secure development processes cover the listed lifecycle topics and that the SO confirms them.
Desk check that secure boot provides integrity and authenticity and that its detection mechanisms suit those guarantees.
Verify on the device that software verification at boot works as documented, possibly by tampering firmware.
Desk check that the documented alert on unauthorized software change suffices and allowed communications are only those needed.
After provoking an unauthorized software change, check alerting and that outbound communication is limited to alerting.
test_cases.outside_procedure_cues: Traffic after a genuine tamper event could be checked for restriction, but the observer cannot know detection occurred.

test_cases.summary: Desk review of documented secure channels carrying personal data to associated services: guarantees, mechanism fit, best-practice crypto per catalogue, no known feasible attack.
test_cases.outside_procedure_cues: Plaintext personal data in traffic would contradict the provision directly.

test_cases.summary: Check on the device that the crypto actually used on channels carrying personal data to associated services matches what the IXIT documents.
test_cases.outside_procedure_cues: Plaintext personal data to cloud endpoints would contradict the provision, but this case only compares with IXIT.

test_cases.summary: Desk review of documented secure channels carrying sensitive personal data to associated services: guarantees, mechanism fit, best-practice crypto per catalogue, no known feasible attack.
test_cases.outside_procedure_cues: Plaintext sensitive personal data in traffic would contradict the provision directly.

test_cases.summary: Check on the device that the crypto actually used on channels carrying sensitive personal data to associated services matches what the IXIT documents.
test_cases.outside_procedure_cues: Plaintext sensitive data (e.g. unencrypted camera streams) would contradict the provision, but this case only compares with IXIT.

test_cases.summary: Check sensor documentation is reachable and understandable for lay users, and that all obvious sensors are documented.
test_cases.outside_procedure_cues: Traffic patterns such as audio or video uploads can hint at sensors in use.

test_cases.summary: Judge whether the SO-declared resilience mechanisms suit network and power outages and meet their stated guarantees.
test_cases.outside_procedure_cues: Reconnection and event-replay bursts after natural WAN or power outages hint at buffering or retry mechanisms, but not their declared guarantees.

test_cases.summary: Cut network and power to the device and check resilience behaviour matches the SO description.
test_cases.outside_procedure_cues: After naturally occurring outages, reconnection loops, DHCP re-requests and resumed cloud sessions show how the device actually recovers.

test_cases.summary: Judge declared resilience mechanisms, including continued local operation without network and clean recovery after power loss.
test_cases.outside_procedure_cues: Post-outage traffic shows whether the device reconnects at all, which hints at recovery design but not at the declared mechanism types.

test_cases.summary: Induce network and power loss; check the device keeps working locally and restores connectivity and function as documented.
test_cases.outside_procedure_cues: Declared-behaviour comparison unusable; observed reconnect delays and replayed event uploads could only be compared with expectations, not the IXIT.

test_cases.summary: Judge whether declared per-interface resilience measures give orderly connection and avoid mass reconnection.
test_cases.outside_procedure_cues: Fleet-level load balancing or batched update notifications are invisible from one home.

test_cases.summary: Verify the declared resilience measures, especially against simultaneous mass reconnection, e.g. by sniffing connection setup and teardown.
test_cases.outside_procedure_cues: TCP setup/teardown conformance and reconnect timing (jitter, backoff, server spread) are visible in traffic, especially after outages the observer cannot cause.

test_cases.summary: Check at least one security examination of telemetry is declared and that the telemetry suits detecting security anomalies.
test_cases.outside_procedure_cues: Periodic uploads to telemetry-like endpoints suggest telemetry exists, but its examination is invisible.

test_cases.summary: Judge whether a simple user-data erasure function exists, is adequate, and covers personal data, configuration and user keys.
test_cases.outside_procedure_cues: Post-reset traffic reusing user-set hostnames or account sessions would hint at incomplete erasure but is not used here.

test_cases.summary: Create user data, run each erase function, check interaction matches and data is gone; check users cannot delete others' data.
test_cases.outside_procedure_cues: Interaction-consistency bullet unusable; observed reset sequence (re-provisioning traffic) could otherwise be compared with the declared flow.

test_cases.summary: Judge whether a simple function deletes personal data held by associated services and covers all such services.
Create personal data on associated services, run deletion, check interaction and that the service no longer holds it.
test_cases.outside_procedure_cues: Continued encrypted sessions to the same service after a user's deletion request hint at remaining accounts but reveal nothing about stored data.

test_cases.summary: Check the user documentation covers every deletion function concisely with all steps, by following it.
test_cases.outside_procedure_cues: Coverage bullet unusable: comparing published instructions with the declared function list needs the IXIT.

test_cases.summary: Run each deletion function per documentation and check the user receives a clear confirmation of deletion.
Judge whether each declared user decision during setup/maintenance is necessary and has a secure default.
Trigger each user decision and check it is prominent, understandable, and as declared.
test_cases.outside_procedure_cues: Setup-phase traffic (provisioning access point, pairing bursts) marks when decisions occur but not how they are presented.

test_cases.summary: Set up the device following secure-setup documentation; check every security-relevant decision is covered with a recommendation.
test_cases.outside_procedure_cues: Coverage bullet unusable as written; observed security-relevant features (UPnP, local APIs) absent from the guide would otherwise indicate gaps.

test_cases.summary: Judge whether setup-check and maintenance-check documentation covers every needed step and parameter.
Configure the device securely then insecurely and check the documented checks correctly tell the two apart.
test_cases.outside_procedure_cues: Traffic can independently reveal insecure states (plaintext services, outdated firmware banners) that a correct user check should flag.

test_cases.summary: Check each user interface has a declared input validation method and that it is effective.
Check all user interfaces are declared and try malformed input (fuzzing, web scanning) to see validation holds.
test_cases.outside_procedure_cues: A plaintext web UI seen in traffic reveals interfaces and error pages but not validation behaviour.

test_cases.summary: Check each network-accessible logical interface has a declared input validation method that is effective.
test_cases.outside_procedure_cues: Observed listening services and protocols identify which interfaces receive network input, without revealing validation.

test_cases.summary: Fuzz or scan network interfaces to test validation; check all network interfaces are declared.
test_cases.outside_procedure_cues: Observed listening services and protocols could reveal network interfaces missing from the public manual.

test_cases.summary: Judge whether the way personal data processing is documented gives clear information on what, why, who and how long.
Check consumer-facing information on personal data processing is clear and matches the declared data categories, purposes, parties and retention.
test_cases.outside_procedure_cues: Match-with-declaration bullet unusable; observed destinations and plaintext fields could otherwise be set against the declared processing.

test_cases.summary: Judge whether opt-in consent for consent-based processing is described as free, obvious and explicit.
Check consent is actually obtained as the SO describes for each consent-based data category.
test_cases.outside_procedure_cues: Analytics or advertising traffic beginning before setup completes would indicate processing without opt-in, but is not usable here.

test_cases.summary: Judge whether the SO describes how consent can be withdrawn at any time via device/service settings.
Check consent can be withdrawn as described for each consent-based data category.
test_cases.outside_procedure_cues: Analytics flows persisting after a user withdraws consent would be a strong cue, but cannot be used.

test_cases.summary: Judge whether the device provides a means to store consent information as declared.
Check stored consent information is as described for each consent-based data category.
Judge whether personal data within declared telemetry is necessary for the stated purpose.
Judge whether the telemetry documentation lets consumers learn about telemetry processing.
test_cases.outside_procedure_cues: Observed telemetry endpoints confirm telemetry exists, strengthening a missing-documentation finding.

test_cases.summary: Obtain the telemetry information and check it matches the declared purposes and describes what is collected, use, recipients and purposes.
test_cases.outside_procedure_cues: Bullets on matching the declaration are unusable; observed telemetry could otherwise be compared with declared purposes.

test_cases.summary: Judge necessity of each personal data category, reasonableness of its retention, and suitability of its disposal process.
test_cases.outside_procedure_cues: Retention and disposal (b,c) have no passive evidence.

test_cases.summary: Create personal data, find data collected not created by the user, judge its necessity, and check deletion when no longer needed.
For data used only for aggregation, judge minimal collection, early aggregation and minimal retention.
Create data meant for aggregation and check the aggregation mechanism behaves as declared.
test_cases.outside_procedure_cues: Plaintext uploads of raw per-event records, where public docs describe aggregation, would hint at non-minimal collection.

test_cases.summary: Judge whether declared anonymization technologies are used and appropriate across collection, processing and storage.
Create data meant for anonymization and check anonymization works as declared.
test_cases.outside_procedure_cues: Identifiers visible in plaintext uploads of data that public docs call anonymized would contradict the published claim.
